title: Privilege Briefs: Compact action panels for quick permissions decisions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, glanceable panel pattern ("privilege briefs") for the Redwood Console that surfaces a user's effective permissions, recent access events, and one-click remediation/rollout actions. The pattern is intended for workspace admins and on-call engineers who need to make fast, low-risk decisions during incidents or audits without drilling into the full Roles page.
background: Current console flows require multiple clicks to verify who has access, correlate that access with recent audit events, and then enact rollouts or temporary remediations. Support and on-call teams report friction when responding to alerts: they want a concise surface that combines permissions + recent activity + recommended actions with clear cost and SLO impact for enabling/disabling routes.
goals: Reduce time-to-decision for permission-related incidents by providing a single compact surface
Prevent accidental overbroad permission changes by showing explicit who/what/when with rollback affordances
Surface cost signal when recommending enabling higher-cost routes or model variants
Be usable across Org and Workspace contexts and fit inside the Alerts, Rollouts, and Audit Log panes
ux_proposal: A horizontally stacked card (72–96px height) that shows: left: identity pill + role badges; center: summarized effective permissions (readable sentences, max 2 lines) and top 3 recent audit events with time and action; right: a compact action column with primary quick action (Temporarily remove / Grant scope-limited role), secondary (Start canary rollback / Schedule review), and a small cost delta badge when action affects dedicated capacity or model routing. Hover expands to an inline drawer with links to full Role detail, audit timeline, and cost estimator.
accessibility_considerations: Text must have 4.5:1 contrast on badges and primary actions
Keyboard focus should allow arrow-key traversal between brief cards and Enter to expand inline drawer
Action confirmations use accessible modal with clear consequences and undo within 2 minutes
tradeoffs: Compact summaries limit visible permission detail; risk of missing edge-case entitlements — mitigated by one-click expand to full role detail
Showing cost deltas inline may distract during critical incident triage; we prioritize a subdued neutral color with tooltip rather than aggressive warnings
Inline remediation reduces context-switching but requires tighter guardrails (confirmations, audit logging) to avoid accidental changes
review_feedback: PM (Miguel Torres): Love the one-line recommendation; request adding a 'confidence' score when the UI suggests a recommended action based on audit heuristics
Eng (Leah Kim): Need API contract changes to return recent effective events and cost delta in a single endpoint (ENG-2419). Also confirm rate limits for inline rollouts
Security (Omar Rahman): Require security_review_required and add an allowlist gate for any actions that touch 'platform-admin' scope
Design critique (Claire Nguyen): Consider replacing the inline cost badge with a tiny flame icon + tooltip when cost delta > 15% to reduce visual noise
decisions: Keep default view compact (max 2 lines of permission summary) with hover-expansion; do not show full policy JSON inline
Show a cost delta badge only when action affects dedicated capacity or model routing and delta > 10%
All quick actions require inline confirmation and will append an annotated audit entry automatically
acceptance_criteria: Prototype built and tested in Figma with example Org and Workspace contexts
Design handoff includes tokenized sizes/colors and copy guidelines for summaries and action labels
Security sign-off recorded in ticket and allowlist workflow defined
UX tests with 6 engineers on-call show median decision time improvement vs baseline by >= 30% (prototype task script attached)
